learning_outcomes.text: Know the principles of construction technology, attending to the constructive logic of its load-bearing and foundation systems, as well as the geotechnical characteristics of the ground.
Know the materials used in building processes, their properties and applications.
Know the different types of machinery used in construction processes and their operation.
Know the enclosure and finishing systems in industrial buildings.
Ability to express basic constructive details and construction processes with precision and clarity.
Ability to make measurements and budgets in industrial building projects and works.
Know the management and certification procedures necessary in construction works.
Be able to carry out certifications, audits, verifications, tests and reports in the field of industrial construction.
Know the responsibilities and obligations of the agents involved in the building process.
Know the administrative and management procedures for the building project and work.
Know the deontological norms applicable to the professional activity of the industrial technical engineer.

syllabus_topics: Study and description of the machinery involved in construction.
Description of the preliminary works before the start of the construction. Ground conditioning and drainage. Foundation systems and ground containment.
Exterior enclosure systems and their selection criteria.
Description of distribution and finishing systems.
Study of safety and risk prevention in construction.
Civil and criminal liability. The Building Regulation Law and professional competencies.
teaching_methods: Acquisition of theoretical knowledge through lectures, preparing cases that will anticipate the content to be developed.
Practical sessions to enhance practical learning. After each session, autonomous development of a work will be requested to form the portfolio created by the student.
Tutorials to review the acquisition of knowledge and the development of the works.
Visits to buildings and civil works under construction and/or completed.

assessment_methods.method: Completion and oral presentation of a work describing how a building or civil work was constructed, with special emphasis on its constructive details and the techniques used in its construction. The scope of the explanation will cover the complete construction, from the foundation to the roof, including the constructive resolution of the structure and the thermal envelope of the building.
Critical and active participation in class development.
Collection of notes and follow-up notes from the theoretical and practical classes.

assessment_rules: Students will be evaluated through a progressive evaluation procedure. Absence from more than 8 hours of class leads to the impossibility of continuous evaluation. Orthographic errors in assignments and evaluation tests will be penalized with a maximum of 10% of the test grade. Alternatively, students may opt for a global evaluation consisting of a theoretical-practical exam. Academic fraud can lead to a failing grade (0) for the test or subject.
